worktree: modified: forensics/memory-safety/campaign/safe-c33/state.json, forensics/tools/consumer_closure.py, this receipt. No Rust source changed; no commit or push made.
scope: The 9 reachable files / 11 production obligations that the openssh consumer closure could not classify (UNKNOWN_MECHANISM). Each obligation is classified individually; no ownership reconstruction is claimed and no discharge is manufactured.

registry.read_by: forensics/tools/consumer_closure.py (build_receipt loads state.json as --state; mechanism_for resolves the mechanism per obligation)

added.purpose: Cross-cutting ABI-edge contract mechanism for unsafe extern "C" fn callback definitions, unsafe extern "C" {} shim blocks, and internal unsafe fn adapters whose caller contract is a raw C/ABI contract rather than an ownership interior.

added.field: obligation_mechanisms[] (11 records keyed by file, line, kind)
added.purpose: Exact per-site classification. These records only classify; the mechanism's own state and receipts still decide whether anything is discharged.

added.field: consumer_closure.py: load_obligation_mechanisms() and the optional obligation/obligation_mechanisms arguments of mechanism_for()
added.purpose: Read the per-site records before the file-level converted_files_on_branch/directory rules. The existing self-test still passes and now covers the override and its absence.

registry.why_not_converted_files_on_branch: Adding these files to converted_files_on_branch would assert they were converted. They were not. Per-site records avoid both that false claim and the coarser directory-rule misattribution of heterogeneous files (dso/mod.rs, eng_table.rs, async_posix.rs, passphrase.rs).

new_mechanism.justification: The campaign already treats the affected surfaces as callback/loader boundaries and defers them (M52: eng_dyn/eng_table excluded as loader/callback boundaries; M41: async fibre/ucontext shim; M29: init/atexit callback boundaries; M83: ui_openssl console callback boundary). No ownership mechanism can state a callback's caller contract, so routing these obligations to ENGINE/UI/CONF/async ownership mechanisms would manufacture a discharge path that does not exist. One cross-cutting mechanism for the ABI-edge function contract is the smallest honest class.
new_mechanism.discharge_requirement: A per-site # Safety contract naming the caller, the pointer/alias/initialisation preconditions it must establish, and caller-closure evidence, reviewed at BOUNDARY. An ownership receipt in another mechanism does not discharge an ABI-edge function contract.

obligations.rationale: cb is the X509_STORE_set_verify_cb callback. The caller that establishes ctx liveness/type is the crypto/x509 store-context verifier, which X509_VERIFY_POLICY owns. The existing mechanism does not enumerate this consumer-side app callback, so no discharge is implied.

Declarations of the C-side ucontext_t shim in src/async/arch/async_ucontext.c. Layout/size/alignment stay on the C side of the ABI. No existing ownership mechanism covers a platform shim; the same file's allocator and lock sites belong to other mechanisms. Classified at the ABI edge, not as async-stack ownership.

The body is the ERR_add_error_data adapter: its unsafe obligations are the libc dlerror() string and the openssl_rs_err_add_data append, both ERR-owned. ERR-1 is SAFETY_DISCHARGED at mechanism scope, but its declared surface does not name this site; the closure therefore returns UNKNOWN, not DISCHARGED.

dynamic_finish is an ENGINE method callback installed through the ENGINE finish-function slot. No ENGINE ownership mechanism exists, and ENGINE ownership would not by itself state this callback's caller contract.

engine_pile_hash is the OPENSSL_LH_new hash callback over a stored ENGINE_PILE. The lhash representation and callback-invocation contract are in crypto/lhash, which RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP declares. RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP is UNSAFE_OPEN: reconstruction is required before any discharge; this mapping is not a soundness claim.
look_str_cb is an ENGINE_TABLE_DOALL_CB callback invoked by engine_table_doall under the engine lock. No ENGINE ownership mechanism exists; the obligation is the callback's ABI contract.

do_ui_passphrase is an internal unsafe fn whose raw-pointer caller contract (pass/pass_len writability, prompt_info NUL-termination, ui_method validity) is documented only at block level. It is a UI/passphrase ABI-edge helper, not an ownership interior; its secret buffers are separately owned by the allocator seam.

ssl_module_free_thunk is the CONF_module_add finish callback. The CONF module-registry callback contract is an ABI edge; no CONF ownership mechanism exists. The existing B7-CONF-2 receipt covers the diagnostic builders, not this thunk.
ui_new_method_data is a CRYPTO_EX_new callback called through a function pointer by the ex-data machinery. No UI ownership mechanism exists; classified at the ABI edge.

ui_dup_method_data is a CRYPTO_EX_dup callback that receives and replaces the ex-data slot pointer. Its pointer-to-pointer contract is the ex-data ABI edge, not an ownership interior owned by an existing mechanism.
ui_close is a UI_METHOD close callback installed on the wrapper method. No UI ownership mechanism exists; the obligation is the method-table callback contract.

mechanisms_with_obligations.statement: UNSAFE_OPEN. Reconstruction is required before any discharge. The mapping records the owner of the lhash callback contract; it does not assert that the mechanism is sound.
UNSAFE_OPEN. The mechanism is new and has no reconstruction or receipt; every site still needs its # Safety contract and caller closure.

unsafe_open.asn1_ocsp: Not touched by this mapping. It remains UNSAFE_OPEN; any obligation mapped there would require reconstruction before discharge.

closure_rerun.changes_explained: The 11 former unmapped obligations are now classified: 4 became BLOCKED because their files have a CONTRACTED boundary receipt and the mapped mechanism is not SAFETY_DISCHARGED at the site; 7 remained UNKNOWN because their files have no boundary receipt (the adjudicator checks that before the mechanism state). DISCHARGED stayed 0.

non_claims: Classification is not discharge. DISCHARGED remains 0 and no mechanism here is SAFETY_DISCHARGED at these sites.
No ownership reconstruction was performed for ENGINE, UI, CONF, async, passphrase or the C ABI edge.
C_ABI_CONTRACT is a contract-completeness mechanism, not an ownership mechanism; it does not claim the data those callbacks operate on is safely owned.

The four BLOCKED obligations are blocked by the mapped mechanism state, not by a defect finding; their CONTRACTED boundary receipts do not cover the obligation at issue (conf_ssl thunk in particular).
The seven UNKNOWN obligations remain unknown because their files have no boundary-sweep receipt; the mechanism classification does not substitute for that missing receipt.
No family is SAFE_COMPATIBLE: the closure remains REFUSED on MISSING_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT and UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION.
